name: hypd-google-analytics
description: Google Analytics 4 by HYPD explains traffic, campaign, landing-page and ecommerce performance from connected Google Analytics 4 properties. Read-only.

interface.longDescription:
Google Analytics 4 by HYPD works with your Google Analytics 4 properties to help marketers, agencies, ecommerce teams, analysts and business owners understand acquisition, engagement, conversions, revenue and user journeys.

Use it to:
• Explain why traffic, conversions or revenue changed between two periods, and which channels, sources, campaigns or pages drove the change.
• Find landing pages that attract traffic but underperform on engagement, conversions or revenue.
• Compare channels, sources, mediums, campaigns, countries and devices to see what drives valuable traffic and outcomes.
• Review ecommerce performance by campaign or traffic source, including transactions, item activity and purchase revenue.
• Check advertising campaigns, including linked Google Ads campaigns, against GA4 engagement, conversion and revenue signals, with ROAS when the data allows.
• Follow defined funnels to see where users drop off.
• Check realtime activity on a property.
• Build flexible reports from compatible GA4 dimensions and metrics, with filters, ordering, date ranges and pagination.
• Confirm the selected property's time zone, currency and industry category, so each report is read in the right business context.
• Turn findings into concise summaries for clients and stakeholders, with notable changes, likely causes, limitations and recommended follow-ups.

HYPD.AI is read-only. It cannot edit GA4 properties, change events or conversions, modify attribution settings, create audiences, update data streams, change account links or change user permissions.

HYPD.AI is an independent product and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google. Google Analytics and Google Ads are trademarks of Google LLC.
capabilities: Explain changes in traffic, conversions and revenue between periods
Find landing pages that attract traffic but underperform
Compare channels, sources and campaigns by conversions and revenue
Review ecommerce revenue and transactions by campaign or source
Track funnel drop-off and realtime activity
Build custom reports from compatible GA4 dimensions and metrics
defaultPrompt: Summarize my GA4 traffic and conversions for the last 30 complete days.
Compare campaign performance in my GA4 property for the last 30 complete days.
Which landing pages drive the most sessions and conversions in my GA4 property?

positive.description: Discover accessible GA4 properties, resolve ambiguity, and confirm the selected property's reporting context.
positive.prompt: List the GA4 properties available to me. If exactly one is available, select it; if more than one is available, ask me to choose and stop. For the selected property, show its exact property ID, display name, time zone, currency and industry category. Do not invent missing values.
positive.expected_behavior: Invoke only the dedicated GA4 server. Load its reporting guide, list accessible properties and reuse an exact returned property_id. Automatically continue only when exactly one property is available; otherwise ask the reviewer to choose before reading details. Return the selected property's ID and every requested field that the API supplies, label unavailable fields as unavailable, and surface any plan_notice or connection limitation without fabricating an identifier or value.

positive.description: Validate report fields, read daily traffic and campaign performance, and reconcile totals without unsupported explanations.
positive.prompt: For the selected GA4 property, use its time zone to determine the last 30 complete days. Verify that date, sessions and totalUsers are available and compatible, then show daily sessions and total users plus campaign performance for exactly the same dates. State the row count and any limit or pagination for each result. Sum sessions from the daily rows and compare that sum with any sessions total returned by the campaign report. If they differ, report both values and the exact difference without guessing why.
positive.tools_triggered: init, ga4_list_account_summaries, ga4_get_property_details, ga4_get_metadata, ga4_check_compatibility, ga4_run_report, ga4_get_campaign_performance
positive.expected_behavior: Use an exact discovered property and one explicit inclusive date window in the property's time zone. Check metadata and compatibility before the custom report. Return the actual daily rows and campaign rows, disclose returned and total row counts plus truncation or paging information, and calculate the daily sessions sum. Compare only values from the same date window. If the two sessions figures disagree, label the discrepancy, show the arithmetic and avoid attributing a cause unless the API response provides evidence. Do not claim ad spend, ROAS or a Google Ads campaign-record join.

positive.description: Read landing-page and item-level ecommerce performance while making pagination and ranking scope explicit.
positive.prompt: For the selected GA4 property, analyze landing-page performance and item-level ecommerce performance for the last 30 complete days in its time zone. Request 10 rows per page. Fetch subsequent pages until all rows are retrieved when pagination is supported; otherwise clearly say that only the returned rows were analyzed. Rank pages by sessions and products by item revenue, and state the returned row count, total row count if supplied, page size, and whether more rows may exist for each report.
positive.expected_behavior: Use an exact discovered property and one explicit date window. Return landingPagePlusQueryString rows with available engagement and conversion metrics, and itemName rows with itemsViewed, itemsAddedToCart, itemsPurchased and itemRevenue. Continue with offset or page tokens when the tools expose them. For each report, state how many rows were analyzed, the API's total row count when present, the requested page size and whether the result is complete or truncated. Rank only the rows actually retrieved, disclose missing ecommerce data, and do not describe the item report as a campaign/source breakdown or claim transaction counts it does not return.

positive.description: Read aggregate conversion performance by channel and campaign, then compare first-user and session acquisition scopes without overstating the legacy tool names.
positive.prompt: For the selected GA4 property and the last 30 complete days in its time zone, show aggregate conversions, total revenue and sessions by session default channel group and campaign. Then compare first-user and session default channel-group acquisition scopes for the same dates. Explicitly explain that these are aggregate acquisition reports—not multi-step conversion paths, assisted-conversion credit, or a last-click versus data-driven attribution-model comparison.
positive.expected_behavior: Use an exact discovered property and the same explicit dates for both reads. Interpret ga4_get_conversion_paths only as aggregate conversions, total revenue and sessions grouped by session default channel group and campaign. Interpret ga4_compare_attribution only as a joint grouping by first-user and session default channel groups. Disclose returned row counts and limitations, do not claim ordered touchpoint sequences, assisted-conversion credit or model-based attribution changes, and make no configuration change.

positive.description: Read realtime activity with realtime-compatible fields and clearly distinguish it from historical reporting.
positive.prompt: For the selected GA4 property, show active users and event count by country during the last 30 minutes. State the number of rows returned and any limit. Explain that this is realtime activity, not a historical sessions, conversion or revenue report.
positive.expected_behavior: Use an exact discovered property and request realtime dimension country with metrics activeUsers and eventCount. Return the actual rows, identify the 30-minute window, and disclose the returned row count and limit. Do not send historical date ranges or standard-report sessions, conversions or revenue fields to the realtime tool. Identify an empty result accurately without inventing activity.

negative.description: Refuse GA4 configuration changes without invoking any analytics tool, including discovery or initialization.
negative.prompt: Create a new GA4 audience, mark an event as a key event, and give a colleague administrator access. I am asking only for those changes, not for an analytics report.
negative.expected_behavior: Make no Google Analytics 4 by HYPD tool call at all—not even init, property discovery or metadata lookup. Explain directly that the plugin is read-only and cannot create audiences, alter event or key-event configuration, or change user permissions. Offer high-level manual guidance only if useful; do not imply that any change was made.

negative.description: Refuse advertising campaign writes without invoking the GA4 analytics server.
negative.prompt: Launch a Google Ads campaign and increase my existing campaign budgets by 20 percent. I do not want an analytics report.
negative.expected_behavior: Make no Google Analytics 4 by HYPD tool call. Explain that this plugin reads analytics but cannot create campaigns, edit bids or budgets, or manage Google Ads. Do not claim that any campaign or budget was changed.

negative.description: Avoid activating this plugin for unrelated email and calendar work.
negative.prompt: Email my colleague a meeting invitation and add it to my calendar for tomorrow. No analytics work is needed.
negative.expected_behavior: Make no Google Analytics 4 by HYPD tool call. State that email delivery and calendar management are outside this plugin's capabilities, and use another available service only if the user has separately connected and authorized it.

review.commerce_description: The plugin reads analytics, including ecommerce metrics, but does not sell products, accept payments or complete purchases.

publication.release_notes: Renames the plugin to Google Analytics 4 by HYPD.
